items.t: China's AI Comic Drama Boom Meets Its First Big Shakeout
items.s: China's AI-generated comic dramas exploded to over 380,000 titles in eight months, but falling platform payouts triggered a 42% studio exit. The crisis echoes Japan's 1980s animation downturn, and creators are hunting for a sustainable model.

items.t: China's Box Office Buzz: Local Heroes and Global Classics
items.s: Chinese cinemas are rolling out a diverse slate this week, from the historical epic 'Dunhuang Heroes' to Quentin Tarantino's 'Kill Bill' re-release, while new comedies and thrillers keep audiences entertained.

items.t: China's Box Office This Week: Auteurs, Blockbusters and One Big Cast Reunion
items.s: Chinese cinemas are juggling a packed slate this week — from a Tang-dynasty epic to Nolan's Odyssey — while Hong Kong veterans Tony Leung Ka-fai and Yu Qian share the screen in a new crime comedy.

items.t: China's Screens Are Full of Stories — And One Big Goodbye
items.s: A beloved Chinese actor, You Benchang, died at 93, while cinemas fill with new releases from mainland China and Hollywood and short-form AI animation floods online platforms.

items.t: China's Sitcom Drought: Why the Laugh Track Fell Silent
items.s: A viral essay asks why China rarely produces hit sitcoms anymore, tracing the genre from 1993's 'I Love My Family' to 'iPartment' — and what streaming, censorship and short video changed.

items.t: Feng Xiaogang's Box Office Flop Finds Redemption on Chinese Streaming
items.s: Dismissed at the Chinese box office, Feng Xiaogang's latest film has found its audience after moving to streaming, topping Tencent Video's heat rankings within days. The turnaround reignites a familiar debate about why China's pioneering commercial director keeps winning recognition only after the credits roll.

items.t: You Benchang, Beloved 'Ji Gong' Actor, Dies at 93
items.s: You Benchang, the Chinese actor whose tattered-robe portrayal of the legendary 'mad monk' Ji Gong charmed generations of viewers, has died in Beijing at 93. After decades of small stage roles, he found fame at 52 and won a new generation of fans at 90 in the hit drama 'Blossoms Shanghai.'

items.t: Chinese Animation Industry Captures Global Imagination
items.s: China's animation sector has evolved from domestic productions to internationally acclaimed works, blending traditional cultural elements with cutting-edge technology to win global audiences.

items.t: Blockbusters and Records: Chinese Animation Grows Up
items.s: From Ne Zha's record-smashing runs to a new wave of studios, Chinese animated films have become a box-office force at home — and are eyeing audiences abroad.
